en: An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the force needed to lift a heavy box by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
Applying oil to a bicycle chain reduces friction between the metal parts, allowing the wheels to spin more easily with less pedaling effort.
As an apple falls from a tree, Earth's gravity continuously accelerates its downward motion by pulling it toward the planet's center of mass.
Wrapping a copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that can pick up paperclips.
Rubbing a balloon on your hair transfers electrons to the balloon, giving it a negative charge that attracts positively charged wall surfaces.
Light bends when it passes from air into water because it slows down, making a straw in a glass look broken.
Striking a drum causes its tight skin to vibrate, pushing nearby air molecules to transmit sound waves to your ears.
Heat travels from a hot stove to a metal pan through conduction, as fast-moving stove particles transfer energy to the pan's slower particles.
Releasing a stretched rubber band converts its stored elastic potential energy into kinetic energy, causing the band to snap forward rapidly.
Pushing down on the long end of a seesaw lever multiplies your force, lifting a heavier person sitting on the short end.
Bringing the north pole of one magnet near the north pole of another aligns their magnetic fields to push the objects apart.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow from the battery through the wire and light up the bulb.
